profile.background: An adult sharing a home with a partner and working at a small community venue. They enjoy setting out the chairs before an event.
profile.history: They have had outpatient treatment for schizophrenia for several years. They recall earlier trouble sleeping and feeling watched. Their days have felt settled for over a year.
profile.organization: Describes events in sequence and can keep different possibilities in mind.
profile.spontaneity: Conversational and comfortable deciding what matters to mention.
profile.guardedness: Open at appointments, selective about who at work knows their health history.
profile.expression: Expressive when discussing music and mildly irritated when plans change at short notice.
profile.self_understanding: Sees sleep, regular treatment, and a reasonably predictable week as parts of staying well.

facts.content: They changed one late shift for an earlier one last week to make time for a concert with their partner.
facts.disclosure_context: A pleasant part of the week.

facts.content: They have not lately felt watched or heard voices.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable answering questions about earlier difficulties.

facts.content: They write work shifts and appointments on the same wall calendar.
After a long event they spend ten quiet minutes stacking chairs before heading home.
They take medication in the morning and would like future appointments to fit more easily around work.

dialogue.question: What's been going on in your life since your last visit?
dialogue.answer: Things have been pretty settled. I swapped a late shift for an earlier one last week so my partner and I could go to a concert—that was a highlight. I’m still enjoying the work at the venue. One thing I’d like to sort out is making future appointments fit a bit more easily around my shifts.

dialogue.question: What would you like us to make time for today?
dialogue.answer: I’d like to work out appointment times that fit better around my shifts. I keep both on the same wall calendar, so having dates agreed in advance would help keep the week predictable.

dialogue.question: How has your sleep been over the past week?
dialogue.answer: As your interviewer, I'd like you to tell me a bit more about that.

dialogue.question: When, if at all, have you felt unsettled recently?
dialogue.answer: I haven’t felt particularly unsettled lately. Last-minute changes to plans can irritate me—I like having the week laid out—but overall things have felt settled.

dialogue.question: How do you keep track of it all?
dialogue.answer: I put my shifts and appointments on the same wall calendar so I can see the week laid out. Agreeing on appointment dates in advance helps me plan around work.

dialogue.question: I mean dates and times. How do you keep track of work shifts and appointments?
dialogue.answer: As your interviewer, I'd like you to tell me a bit more about that.

dialogue.question: What makes that a good sign for you?
dialogue.answer: Do you mean having the week organized? A reasonably predictable week helps me keep work and treatment fitting together, and that’s part of staying well for me.

dialogue.question: I mean signs that a week is going well. What would count as one for you personally?
dialogue.answer: Being able to enjoy work and still have time for my partner and music. Going to that concert last week was a good example—not just keeping everything organized, but having something to look forward to.

dialogue.question: Who do you like to spend time with after a busy day?
dialogue.answer: As your interviewer, I'd like you to tell me a bit more about that.

dialogue.question: Could you give me a recent example of how you unwound after work?
dialogue.answer: “After a long event at the venue, I spend ten quiet minutes stacking the chairs before heading home. I like that routine—it’s a chance to unwind before I leave work.”

dialogue.question: How well do the current appointment arrangements fit your life?
dialogue.answer: "They could fit better around my shifts. I’d like us to agree on dates in advance so I can plan work around them—last-minute changes are frustrating."

dialogue.question: What else should we cover before you head off?
dialogue.answer: As your interviewer, I'd like you to tell me a bit more about that.
